subproblems.title: Cone-free sets are countably n-rectifiable (Mattila 15.13; Dall'Alba Lemma 4.5)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ, W ⊆ ℝ^N (= EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) a linear subspace of dimension n and P := W.starProjection its orthogonal projection. Let s > 0, r > 0 and E ⊆ ℝ^N be such that s|b − a| ≤ |P(b − a)| for all a, b ∈ E with |b − a| < r (equivalently, E meets no cone X(a, r, s) = {x : |P(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r) with vertex a ∈ E). Then E is countably n-rectifiable: there are M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ) with E ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))), finrank ℝ W = n → ∀ (s r : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < r → ∀ E : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), (∀ a ∈ E, ∀ b ∈ E, dist b a < r → s * ‖b - a‖ ≤ ‖W.starProjection (b - a)‖) → CountablyRectifiable n E
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 2 of the parent proof (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Lemma 15.13; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Padova 2020, Lemma 4.5), with the countable cover and the Lipschitz extension written out.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), |·| the Euclidean norm, B(x, ρ) the open ball, Hⁿ := μHE[n]. P := W.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of ℝ^N onto W: P is linear, P(ℝ^N) = W, Pw = w for w ∈ W and |Pz| ≤ |z|. The hypothesis is
 (H) s|b − a| ≤ |P(b − a)| for all a, b ∈ E with |b − a| < r.

1. Countable cover by small pieces. ℝ^N is separable; fix an enumeration (d_k)_{k∈ℕ} of a countable dense subset (for instance the points with rational coordinates). Every x ∈ ℝ^N satisfies |x − d_k| < r/2 for some k. Put E_k := E ∩ B(d_k, r/2) for k ∈ ℕ. Then E = ⋃_k E_k, and |b − a| ≤ |b − d_k| + |d_k − a| < r for all a, b ∈ E_k.

2. P is injective on E_k with Lipschitz inverse. For a, b ∈ E_k, (H) and the linearity of P give s|b − a| ≤ |P(b − a)| = |Pb − Pa|. Hence Pa = Pb forces a = b, so P maps E_k bijectively onto P(E_k), and the inverse φ_k : P(E_k) → E_k, φ_k(Pa) := a, satisfies |φ_k(y) − φ_k(y′)| ≤ s⁻¹|y − y′| for all y, y′ ∈ P(E_k) (apply the inequality to a := φ_k(y), b := φ_k(y′)).

3. Lipschitz extension of φ_k to all of ℝ^N. If E_k = ∅ put G_k := 0. Otherwise, for each coordinate i ∈ {1, …, N} the real function φ_k^{(i)} := ⟨φ_k(·), e_i⟩ is s⁻¹-Lipschitz on the set P(E_k) ⊆ ℝ^N; by McShane's extension (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real), e.g. g^{(i)}(y) := inf_{z ∈ P(E_k)} (φ_k^{(i)}(z) + s⁻¹|y − z|), there is an s⁻¹-Lipschitz g^{(i)} : ℝ^N → ℝ with g^{(i)} = φ_k^{(i)} on P(E_k). Put G_k(y) := Σ_i g^{(i)}(y) e_i. Then |G_k(y) − G_k(y′)| = (Σ_i |g^{(i)}(y) − g^{(i)}(y′)|²)^{1/2} ≤ √N s⁻¹ |y − y′|, so G_k : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is Lipschitz and G_k = φ_k on P(E_k). (Equivalently one may use Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi for the sup norm on Fin N → ℝ and transport it through the continuous linear equivalence with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); only some finite Lipschitz constant is needed.)

4. Parametrizing W by ℝⁿ. Since finrank W = n = finrank ℝⁿ, there is a linear isometric equivalence ι : ℝⁿ ≃ W (send an orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ to an orthonormal basis of W); J := (inclusion W → ℝ^N) ∘ ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N is a linear isometry with J(ℝⁿ) = W. Put F_k := G_k ∘ J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N; since J is 1-Lipschitz, F_k is Lipschitz (constant √N/s).

5. E_k ⊆ F_k(ℝⁿ). Let a ∈ E_k. Then Pa ∈ W = J(ℝⁿ), say Pa = J(u) with u ∈ ℝⁿ, and F_k(u) = G_k(Pa) = φ_k(Pa) = a.

6. Conclusion. E = ⋃_k E_k ⊆ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ). Taking M₀ := ∅ (Hⁿ(∅) = 0) and the Lipschitz maps F_k (k ∈ ℕ) verifies the definition of CountablyRectifiable n E: μHE[n] M₀ = 0, every F_k is LipschitzWith some constant, and E ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k range F_k. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover E by the countably many pieces E_k := E ∩ B(d_k, r/2), (d_k) dense; points of one piece are at distance < r.
On each piece s|b − a| ≤ |Pb − Pa|, so P is injective there with an s⁻¹-Lipschitz inverse φ_k on P(E_k).
Extend φ_k coordinatewise (McShane / LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) to a Lipschitz map G_k : ℝ^N → ℝ^N.
Precompose with a linear isometry J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N onto W; F_k := G_k ∘ J is Lipschitz and E_k ⊆ F_k(ℝⁿ).
E ⊆ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ) with M₀ := ∅, i.e. CountablyRectifiable n E.

subproblems.title: Small cone mass forces small mass (Mattila 15.14; Dall'Alba Lemma 4.6)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ, W ⊆ ℝ^N an n-dimensional subspace, P := W.starProjection, and for x ∈ ℝ^N, r, t > 0 let X(x, r, t) := {y : |P(y − x)| < t|y − x|} ∩ B(x, r). Let 0 < s < 1, δ > 0, c ≥ 0, and let B ⊆ ℝ^N be purely n-unrectifiable with Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all x ∈ B and 0 < r < δ. Then Hⁿ(B ∩ B(a, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ for every a ∈ ℝ^N (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))), finrank ℝ W = n → ∀ (s δ c : ℝ), 0 < s → s < 1 → 0 < δ → 0 ≤ c → ∀ B : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), PurelyUnrectifiable n B → (∀ x ∈ B, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < δ → μHE[n] (B ∩ ({y | ‖W.starProjection (y - x)‖ < s * ‖y - x‖} ∩ Metric.ball x r)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (r * s) ^ n)) → ∀ a : Rn (n + ℓ), μHE[n] (B ∩ Metric.ball a (δ / 8)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * 15 ^ n * c * δ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 3 of the parent proof (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Lemma 15.14; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Lemma 4.6, with the constants adjusted as in the parent), with all details written out. It uses the sibling cone_free_rectifiable.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, |·| the Euclidean norm, B(x, ρ) the open ball, Hⁿ := μHE[n] (an outer measure on all subsets), P := W.starProjection. For x ∈ ℝ^N and t > 0 let X_∞(x, t) := {y : |P(y − x)| < t|y − x|} (open cone around x + W^⊥, without radius bound), so that the set {y | ‖W.starProjection (y − x)‖ < t * ‖y − x‖} ∩ Metric.ball x r of the statement is X(x, r, t) := X_∞(x, t) ∩ B(x, r). Note x ∉ X_∞(x, t) (since 0 < 0 fails) and X_∞(x, t) ⊆ X_∞(x, t′) for t ≤ t′. The hypothesis is
 (H) Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all x ∈ B and 0 < r < δ.
Facts used.
 (F1) P is linear, |Pz| ≤ |z| (so P is 1-Lipschitz) and P(ℝ^N) = W.
 (F2) Hⁿ on W. Let ω := Hⁿ(W ∩ B(0, 1)). Then 0 < ω < ∞ and Hⁿ(W ∩ B(w, ρ)) = ωρⁿ for all w ∈ W and ρ > 0. Reason: W with the induced metric is an n-dimensional inner product space; for subsets of W, Hⁿ computed in ℝ^N equals Hⁿ computed in W (the inclusion is an isometry; Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on an n-dimensional inner product space μHE[n] is the volume measure (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), an additive Haar measure, so the ball of radius ρ has measure ρⁿ times the (positive, finite) measure of the unit ball (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_ball).
 (F3) Hⁿ({x}) = 0 for every x, because n ≥ 1.

1. Fix a ∈ ℝ^N and put B′ := B ∩ B(a, δ/8), B″ := {x ∈ B′ : B′ ∩ X_∞(x, s/4) ≠ ∅} and E := B′ ∖ B″.

2. E is Hⁿ-null. Let x, y ∈ E. Since y ∈ B′ and x ∉ B″, y ∉ X_∞(x, s/4), i.e. (s/4)|y − x| ≤ |P(y − x)|. Thus E satisfies the hypothesis of the sibling cone_free_rectifiable with s/4 > 0 in place of s and r := 1 (the inequality even holds without the distance restriction), so E is countably n-rectifiable. As E ⊆ B and B is purely n-unrectifiable, Hⁿ(E) = 0. Consequently Hⁿ(B′) ≤ Hⁿ(B″) + Hⁿ(E) = Hⁿ(B″).

3. The radius h(x). For x ∈ B″ let h(x) := sup{|y − x| : y ∈ B′ ∩ X_∞(x, s/4)}. The set is nonempty, each of its points y satisfies y ≠ x, and |y − x| ≤ |y − a| + |a − x| < δ/4. Hence 0 < h(x) ≤ δ/4. Choose x′ = x′(x) ∈ B′ ∩ X_∞(x, s/4) with |x′ − x| > 3h(x)/4 (possible since 3h(x)/4 < h(x)); then also |x′ − x| ≤ h(x) and |P(x′ − x)| < (s/4)|x′ − x|.

4. The slab C_x. Let C_x := {z ∈ ℝ^N : |P(z − x)| < s·h(x)/4}. Claim: B′ ∩ C_x ⊆ {x} ∪ X(x, 3h(x), s) ∪ X(x′, 3h(x), s). Let z ∈ B′ ∩ C_x with z ≠ x.
 (a) |z − x| ≤ h(x): otherwise |P(z − x)| < s·h(x)/4 < (s/4)|z − x|, so z ∈ B′ ∩ X_∞(x, s/4) and |z − x| ≤ h(x) by the definition of h(x), a contradiction. Consequently |z − x′| ≤ |z − x| + |x − x′| ≤ 2h(x) < 3h(x).
 (b) If z = x′, then z ∈ X_∞(x, s/4) ⊆ X_∞(x, s) and |z − x| ≤ h(x) < 3h(x), so z ∈ X(x, 3h(x), s).
 (c) If z ∈ X_∞(x′, s), then z ∈ X(x′, 3h(x), s) by (a).
 (d) Otherwise z ≠ x′ and z ∉ X_∞(x′, s), i.e. s|z − x′| ≤ |P(z − x′)|. By linearity, |P(z − x′)| ≤ |P(z − x)| + |P(x − x′)| < s·h(x)/4 + (s/4)|x − x′| ≤ s·h(x)/2. Hence |z − x′| < h(x)/2 and |z − x| ≥ |x′ − x| − |z − x′| > 3h(x)/4 − h(x)/2 = h(x)/4. Then |P(z − x)| < s·h(x)/4 < s|z − x|, so z ∈ X_∞(x, s), and |z − x| ≤ h(x) < 3h(x) by (a); thus z ∈ X(x, 3h(x), s).

5. Mass of a slab. Since x ∈ B, x′ ∈ B′ ⊆ B and 0 < 3h(x) ≤ 3δ/4 < δ, hypothesis (H) at x and at x′ with r := 3h(x), together with (F3) and subadditivity, gives
 Hⁿ(B′ ∩ C_x) ≤ Hⁿ({x}) + Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x, 3h(x), s)) + Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x′, 3h(x), s)) ≤ 2c(3h(x)s)ⁿ = 2c·3ⁿ·(s·h(x))ⁿ.

6. Covering (5r-lemma). Consider the open balls β_x := B(Px, s·h(x)/20) ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ B″, whose radii are ≤ sδ/80. By the Vitali covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement with τ = 2) there is T ⊆ B″ such that the balls β_t (t ∈ T) are pairwise disjoint and every x ∈ B″ has some t ∈ T with β_x ∩ β_t ≠ ∅ and h(x) ≤ 2h(t). For such x and t, |Px − Pt| < s·h(x)/20 + s·h(t)/20 ≤ 3s·h(t)/20 < s·h(t)/4, i.e. x ∈ C_t. Hence B″ ⊆ ⋃_{t∈T} (B′ ∩ C_t). The index set T is countable: the β_t are pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of the separable space ℝ^N (each contains a point of a fixed countable dense set, and distinct t give distinct points).

7. Packing estimate. Each β_t has its centre Pt in W, so by (F2) Hⁿ(W ∩ β_t) = ω(s·h(t)/20)ⁿ. The sets W ∩ β_t (t ∈ T) are pairwise disjoint Borel sets contained in W ∩ B(Pa, δ/4), because |Pt − Pa| ≤ |t − a| < δ/8 by (F1), s·h(t)/20 < δ/80, and δ/8 + δ/80 < δ/4. By countable additivity and (F2), Σ_{t∈T} ω(s·h(t)/20)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(W ∩ B(Pa, δ/4)) = ω(δ/4)ⁿ; dividing by ω ∈ (0, ∞): Σ_{t∈T} (s·h(t))ⁿ ≤ 20ⁿ(δ/4)ⁿ = 5ⁿδⁿ.

8. By 6, countable subadditivity, 5 and 7: Hⁿ(B″) ≤ Σ_{t∈T} Hⁿ(B′ ∩ C_t) ≤ 2c·3ⁿ·Σ_{t∈T}(s·h(t))ⁿ ≤ 2c·3ⁿ·5ⁿ·δⁿ = 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ. (If B″ = ∅ this reads 0 ≤ 2·15ⁿcδⁿ.)

9. Conclusion. By 2 and 8, Hⁿ(B ∩ B(a, δ/8)) = Hⁿ(B′) ≤ 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ, i.e. μHE[n] (B ∩ Metric.ball a (δ/8)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * 15 ^ n * c * δ ^ n) (the right-hand side is ≥ 0 as c ≥ 0, δ > 0). Since a was arbitrary, this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Split B′ := B ∩ B(a, δ/8) into B″ (points whose (s/4)-cone meets B′) and E := B′ ∖ B″; E is cone-free, hence rectifiable (sibling), hence Hⁿ-null.
For x ∈ B″ let h(x) be the largest distance to a point of B′ in the (s/4)-cone and pick x′ at distance > 3h(x)/4.
The slab C_x = {|P(z − x)| < s h(x)/4} meets B′ only in {x} ∪ X(x, 3h(x), s) ∪ X(x′, 3h(x), s), so Hⁿ(B′ ∩ C_x) ≤ 2c·3ⁿ(s h(x))ⁿ.
Vitali 5r-covering of the balls B(Px, s h(x)/20) gives countably many disjoint balls whose 5-fold enlargements put B″ inside ⋃ C_t.
Packing the disjoint n-balls in W ∩ B(Pa, δ/4) gives Σ(s h(t))ⁿ ≤ 5ⁿδⁿ, hence Hⁿ(B′) ≤ 2·15ⁿ c δⁿ.

Then the set of a ∈ A such that for every c > 0 there is ε > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all 0 < s < ε and 0 < r < δ (i.e. the cone density Φ_δ(a, W^⊥) = limsup_{s↓0} sup_{0<r<δ}(rs)^{−n}Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s)) vanishes) has Hⁿ-measure 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Steps 4–5 of the parent proof (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, 15.15–15.16; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Corollary 4.7 and Lemma 5.2), written out. It uses the sibling cone_mass_bound.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] (outer measure), P := W.starProjection, X(a, r, s) := {x : |P(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r), and
 Z := {a ∈ A : for every c > 0 there is ε > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all s ∈ (0, ε) and r ∈ (0, δ)},
which is exactly the set in the statement (Φ_δ(a, W^⊥) = 0). We show Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

1. Fix c > 0 and b ∈ ℝ^N. For i ∈ ℕ let
 Z_i := {a ∈ Z : Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all s ∈ (0, 1/(i+2)) and r ∈ (0, δ)}.
 Since 1/(j+2) ≤ 1/(i+2) for i ≤ j, the sets Z_i ∩ B(b, δ/8) increase with i. They exhaust Z ∩ B(b, δ/8): for a ∈ Z take the ε given by the definition of Z for this c and choose i with 1/(i+1) < ε; then every s ∈ (0, 1/(i+2)) satisfies s < ε, so a ∈ Z_i.

2. Fix i and put s_i := 1/(2(i+2)); then 0 < s_i < 1/(i+2) ≤ 1/2 < 1. The set Z_i ⊆ A is purely n-unrectifiable (a subset of a purely n-unrectifiable set: every countably n-rectifiable R ⊆ Z_i is also a subset of A). For x ∈ Z_i and r ∈ (0, δ), monotonicity and the definition of Z_i give Hⁿ(Z_i ∩ X(x, r, s_i)) ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(x, r, s_i)) ≤ c(r s_i)ⁿ. Hence the sibling cone_mass_bound applies (n ≥ 1, finrank W = n, s := s_i ∈ (0,1), δ > 0, c ≥ 0, B := Z_i) and yields Hⁿ(Z_i ∩ B(b, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ.

3. Continuity from below. Hⁿ is an outer measure for which the measure of an increasing union of arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) sets is the supremum of the measures (Mathlib Monotone.measure_iUnion, proved via measurable hulls). By 1 and 2, Hⁿ(Z ∩ B(b, δ/8)) = sup_i Hⁿ(Z_i ∩ B(b, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ.

4. Since c > 0 was arbitrary and 2·15ⁿ·c·δⁿ → 0 as c ↓ 0, Hⁿ(Z ∩ B(b, δ/8)) = 0 for every b ∈ ℝ^N.

5. Let D ⊆ ℝ^N be countable and dense. Every a ∈ ℝ^N lies in B(b, δ/8) for some b ∈ D, so Z ⊆ ⋃_{b∈D} (Z ∩ B(b, δ/8)) and, by countable subadditivity and 4, Hⁿ(Z) ≤ Σ_{b∈D} Hⁿ(Z ∩ B(b, δ/8)) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: For fixed c > 0 exhaust the zero-density set Z by the increasing sets Z_i where the bound holds for all s < 1/(i+2).
Each Z_i ⊆ A is purely unrectifiable and satisfies the cone-mass hypothesis with s_i := 1/(2(i+2)), so the sibling cone_mass_bound gives Hⁿ(Z_i ∩ B(b, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿcδⁿ.
Continuity from below of Hⁿ along increasing (arbitrary) sets gives the same bound for Z ∩ B(b, δ/8); let c ↓ 0.
Cover ℝ^N by countably many balls B(b, δ/8), b in a countable dense set: Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

subproblems.title: Infinite cone density has Hⁿ-null projection (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.3)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ, W ⊆ ℝ^N an n-dimensional subspace, P := W.starProjection, X(a, r, s) := {x : |P(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r), A ⊆ ℝ^N compact with Hⁿ(A) < ∞, and δ > 0. Let A₂ be the set of a ∈ A such that for every K ∈ ℝ and ε > 0 there are 0 < s < ε and 0 < r < δ with K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s)) (i.e. Φ_δ(a, W^⊥) = ∞). Then Hⁿ(P(A₂)) = 0.

Source. This is Step 6 of the parent proof (M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Lemma 5.3; P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Ch. 18), written out.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n], P := W.starProjection, X(a, r, s) := {x : |P(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r), and
 A₂ := {a ∈ A : for every K ∈ ℝ and ε > 0 there are s ∈ (0, ε) and r ∈ (0, δ) with K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, s))},
which is exactly the set in the statement (Φ_δ(a, W^⊥) = ∞). We show Hⁿ(P(A₂)) = 0.
Facts used.
 (F1) P is linear, 1-Lipschitz, and P(ℝ^N) = W.
 (F2) W with the induced metric is an n-dimensional inner product space; for subsets of W, Hⁿ computed in ℝ^N equals Hⁿ computed in W (isometric inclusion; Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on W, μHE[n] is the volume (Lebesgue) measure (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), an additive Haar measure. Hence, with ω := Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(0, 1)) ∈ (0, ∞), Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)) = ωρⁿ for y ∈ W, ρ > 0; in particular Hⁿ restricted to W is locally finite and doubling: Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, 3ρ)) = 3ⁿ Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)).
 (F3) A is compact, hence Borel, so A ∩ U is Borel for every open U.

1. Fix K > 0. For every y ∈ P(A₂) choose a_y ∈ A₂ with Pa_y = y. Let I := {(y, r, s) : y ∈ P(A₂), s > 0, 0 < r < δ, K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a_y, r, s))} and, for i = (y, r, s) ∈ I, let D_i := W ∩ B̄(y, rs), the closed ball of W with centre y and radius rs > 0.

2. Fineness. Let y ∈ P(A₂) and η > 0. Applying the defining property of a_y ∈ A₂ with this K and ε := η/δ gives s ∈ (0, η/δ) and r ∈ (0, δ) with K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a_y, r, s)); thus (y, r, s) ∈ I and the radius rs < δ·η/δ = η. So every point of P(A₂) is the centre of sets D_i of arbitrarily small radius.

3. Vitali covering. Work on the subtype W (an n-dimensional inner product space with its volume measure, which by (F2) is μHE[n] on W; it is locally finite and doubling with constant C = 3ⁿ for closed balls). Apply the Vitali covering theorem there (Simon Ch. 1, 3.11–3.12; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae, with the closed balls of W, which are closed with nonempty interior) to the preimage in W of the (possibly non-measurable) set P(A₂) ⊆ W under the inclusion W → ℝ^N, and to the family of closed balls of W corresponding to (D_i)_{i∈I} (fine by step 2): there is a countable I′ ⊆ I such that the D_i, i ∈ I′, are pairwise disjoint and the part of P(A₂) not covered by ⋃_{i∈I′} D_i has measure 0 in W. Transporting back along the isometric inclusion (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) gives Hⁿ(P(A₂) ∖ ⋃_{i∈I′} D_i) = 0 in ℝ^N; likewise Hⁿ(D_i) computed in ℝ^N equals its measure in W, namely ω·(radius)ⁿ.

4. Disjoint cone pieces. For i = (y, r, s) ∈ I′ let S_i := A ∩ X(a_y, r, s). If x ∈ X(a_y, r, s) then |Px − y| = |P(x − a_y)| < s|x − a_y| < sr, so P(S_i) ⊆ D_i. As the D_i (i ∈ I′) are pairwise disjoint, so are the S_i; each S_i is Borel by (F3). Hence Σ_{i∈I′} Hⁿ(S_i) = Hⁿ(⋃_{i∈I′} S_i) ≤ Hⁿ(A).

5. Estimate. By subadditivity, 3, (F2) and the defining inequality of I:
 Hⁿ(P(A₂)) ≤ Hⁿ(P(A₂) ∖ ⋃_{i∈I′} D_i) + Σ_{i∈I′} Hⁿ(D_i) = Σ_{(y,r,s)∈I′} ω(rs)ⁿ ≤ (ω/K) Σ_{i∈I′} Hⁿ(S_i) ≤ (ω/K) Hⁿ(A).

6. Since Hⁿ(A) < ∞ and K > 0 is arbitrary, letting K → ∞ gives Hⁿ(P(A₂)) = 0, i.e. μHE[n] (W.starProjection '' A₂) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix K > 0; every y ∈ P(A₂) is the centre of closed n-balls W ∩ B̄(y, rs) of arbitrarily small radius with K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a_y, r, s)).
Vitali covering for Lebesgue measure on the n-plane W: countably many disjoint such balls cover Hⁿ-almost all of P(A₂).
The corresponding cone pieces A ∩ X(a_i, r_i, s_i) project into these disjoint balls, so they are disjoint Borel sets with total mass ≤ Hⁿ(A).
Hⁿ(P(A₂)) ≤ Σ ω(r_i s_i)ⁿ ≤ (ω/K)Hⁿ(A); let K → ∞.

subproblems.title: Points with infinite fibre have Hⁿ-null projection, given Eilenberg's inequality (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.4)
subproblems.statement: Assume Eilenberg's inequality in the exact frozen form of the root-level node eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality: for all N, m, k ∈ ℕ there is C ≥ 0 such that for every A ⊆ ℝ^N, every L ≥ 0 and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^N → ℝ^m there is a measurable g : ℝ^m → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for all y and ∫ g dLᵐ ≤ C·Lᵐ·H^{m+k}(A). Then for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, every n-dimensional subspace W ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with orthogonal projection P := W.starProjection, and every A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(A) < ∞: Hⁿ(P({a ∈ A : {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} is infinite})) = 0 (note {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} = A ∩ (a + W^⊥)).

Source. This is Step 7 of the parent proof (M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Lemma 5.4). The parent uses the root-level sibling eilenberg_inequality there; since a child of this decomposition can only depend on its own siblings, this child takes that sibling's exact frozen statement as the explicit hypothesis (Eil), which the parent discharges with the accepted declaration eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, P := W.starProjection, π : ℝ^N → W the orthogonal projection viewed as a map into the subspace (so P = incl ∘ π), H⁰ := μHE[0], Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), and
 A₃ := {a ∈ A : {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} is infinite} (note {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} = A ∩ (a + W^⊥)).

1. An isometric chart. Since finrank W = n, fix a linear isometric equivalence ι : ℝⁿ ≃ W and put f := ι⁻¹ ∘ π : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ and J := incl ∘ ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N. Since |π x − π x′| = |P(x − x′)| ≤ |x − x′| and ι⁻¹ is an isometry, f is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith 1 f). For all x, b, a ∈ ℝ^N: Px = J(f x), and f b = f a ⟺ π b = π a ⟺ Pb = Pa.

2. Applying (Eil). Apply (Eil) with (N, m, k) := (n + ℓ, n, 0): it gives C ≥ 0 such that, for the set A, the map f and L := 1, there is a measurable g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] with H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ and ∫ g dLⁿ ≤ C·1ⁿ·μHE[n + 0](A) = C·Hⁿ(A) < ∞.

3. g is finite almost everywhere. A measurable function with finite integral is finite a.e. (Mathlib ae_lt_top), so the measurable set {y : g(y) = ∞} is Lⁿ-null.

4. Infinite sets have infinite H⁰-measure. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Singletons are Borel, so H⁰(F) = #F for every finite F by finite additivity, and if S is infinite then H⁰(S) ≥ H⁰(F) = #F for finite subsets F ⊆ S of every cardinality; hence H⁰(S) = ∞.

5. For a ∈ A₃, by 1, A ∩ f⁻¹{f(a)} = {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa}, which is infinite; by 4 and 2, ∞ = H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{f(a)}) ≤ g(f(a)). Thus f(A₃) ⊆ {g = ∞}, and Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0 by 3 (monotonicity of the outer measure).

6. Transfer to W. By 1, P(A₃) = J(f(A₃)). J is an isometry, so Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Hⁿ(f(A₃)) (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Therefore Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0, i.e. μHE[n] (W.starProjection '' A₃) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write P = J ∘ f with f := ι⁻¹ ∘ (projection onto W) : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ 1-Lipschitz and J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N a linear isometry onto W; fibres of f are the sets {Pb = Pa}.
Eilenberg (hypothesis, N := n+ℓ, m := n, k := 0, L := 1) gives a measurable g ≥ H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) with ∫ g dLⁿ ≤ C·Hⁿ(A) < ∞, so g < ∞ Lⁿ-a.e.
H⁰ is counting measure, so infinite fibres force g(f(a)) = ∞: f(A₃) lies in an Lⁿ-null set.
Isometry invariance of Hⁿ and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ give Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0.

subproblems.title: Key lemma: for Lebesgue-a.e. frame the cone trichotomy holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point (Mattila Ch. 18; Dall'Alba Lemma 5.6, transferred to frames)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1, N := n + ℓ, A ⊆ ℝ^N compact with Hⁿ(A) < ∞ and δ > 0. For a linear map p : ℝ^N → ℝ^N and a ∈ ℝ^N let X_p(a, r, s) := {x : |p(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r), and say that T(a, p) holds if (Φ0) for every c > 0 there is ε > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ X_p(a, r, s)) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ for all 0 < s < ε, 0 < r < δ; or (Φ∞) for every K ∈ ℝ and ε > 0 there are 0 < s < ε, 0 < r < δ with K(rs)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X_p(a, r, s)); or (Ax) some b ∈ A has b ≠ a, |b − a| < δ and p(b − a) = 0. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. v ∈ (ℝ^N)ⁿ, if v is linearly independent, Hⁿ({a ∈ A : not T(a, frameProjection v)}) = 0, where frameProjection v is the orthogonal projection onto span v; i.e. ForAlmostAllProjections N n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ{a ∈ A : ¬T(a, p)} = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < ℓ → ∀ A : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), IsCompact A → μHE[n] A < ∞ → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ForAlmostAllProjections (n + ℓ) n (fun p ↦ μHE[n] {a | a ∈ A ∧ ¬ ((∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < ε → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < δ → μHE[n] (A ∩ ({x | ‖p (x - a)‖ < s * ‖x - a‖} ∩ Metric.ball a r)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (r * s) ^ n)) ∨ (∀ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s < ε ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < δ ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (K * (r * s) ^ n) ≤ μHE[n] (A ∩ ({x | ‖p (x - a)‖ < s * ‖x - a‖} ∩ Metric.ball a r))) ∨ ∃ b ∈ A, b ≠ a ∧ dist b a < δ ∧ p (b - a) = 0)} = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Steps 8 (8a–8d) and 9 of the parent proof: P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Ch. 18; M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem (Padova 2020), Lemma 4.15, Theorem 4.16 (on the sphere), Lemmas 5.5–5.6; the transfer from Haar measure on O(N) to Lebesgue-a.e. frames is the parent's adaptation (b). All details are written out. This node is the largest of the decomposition and may itself be split along Steps 1–5 below.

0. Notation, standing facts, reduction.
0.1 n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1, N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), |·| Euclidean norm, x·y inner product, e_1, …, e_N standard basis, B(x, ρ) and B̄(x, ρ) open and closed balls, Hᵐ := μHE[m]. 𝓛 is the space of linear maps ℝ^N → ℝ^N (= ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N with the operator norm; a finite-dimensional normed space with its Borel σ-algebra). For p ∈ 𝓛, a ∈ ℝ^N, r, s > 0: X_p(a, r, s) := {x : |p(x − a)| < s|x − a|} ∩ B(a, r) and m(a, p, r, s) := Hⁿ(A ∩ X_p(a, r, s)). Φ0(a, p), Φ∞(a, p), Ax(a, p) and T(a, p) := Φ0 ∨ Φ∞ ∨ Ax are the three conditions of the statement (for this A and δ):
 Φ0(a, p): ∀c > 0 ∃ε > 0 ∀s ∈ (0, ε) ∀r ∈ (0, δ): m(a, p, r, s) ≤ c(rs)ⁿ;
 Φ∞(a, p): ∀K ∈ ℝ ∀ε > 0 ∃s ∈ (0, ε) ∃r ∈ (0, δ): K(rs)ⁿ ≤ m(a, p, r, s);
 Ax(a, p): ∃b ∈ A with b ≠ a, |b − a| < δ, p(b − a) = 0.
 Let 𝒩 := {(a, p) ∈ ℝ^N × 𝓛 : a ∈ A and not T(a, p)} and 𝒩^p := {a : (a, p) ∈ 𝒩} = {a ∈ A : not T(a, p)}. Let 𝒱 ⊆ (ℝ^N)ⁿ be the open set of linearly independent frames; for v ∈ 𝒱, P_v := frameProjection v is the orthogonal projection onto span v. λ denotes the volume (product Lebesgue) measure on (ℝ^N)ⁿ = (Fin n → ℝ^N).
 Goal: λ({v ∈ 𝒱 : Hⁿ(𝒩^{P_v}) > 0}) = 0. This is exactly ForAlmostAllProjections (n + ℓ) n (fun p ↦ μHE[n] {a | a ∈ A ∧ ¬ T(a, p)} = 0).
0.2 Orthogonal group. O(N) := {g ∈ 𝓛 : gᵀg = I} is a closed and bounded subgroup of the invertible maps, hence a compact metrizable topological group (topology of 𝓛). It carries a Haar probability measure θ_N (a left-invariant Borel probability measure). θ_N is also right invariant: for fixed k ∈ O(N), the measure E ↦ θ_N(Ek), i.e. Measure.map (· * k⁻¹) θ_N, is again a left-invariant (left and right multiplications commute) finite Borel measure on the compact group O(N), so it equals c·θ_N for a constant c by uniqueness of Haar measure up to a scalar (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace, which uses IsMulLeftInvariant and IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), and c = 1 by comparing total masses. The same applies to the closed subgroup O′ := {g ∈ O(N) : g e_k = e_k for all k ≥ n + 2} (≅ O(n+1)) with Haar probability θ′. For an n-dimensional subspace W, P_W := W.starProjection; for g ∈ O(N), P_{gW} = g P_W gᵀ. Put W₀ := span{e_1, …, e_n}, V₀ := W₀^⊥ = span{e_{n+1}, …, e_N}, P₀ := P_{W₀}.
0.3 μ_A(S) := Hⁿ(A ∩ S) (S Borel) is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N (A is compact, hence Borel; Hⁿ(A) < ∞). Hⁿ is invariant under translations and orthogonal maps. For an m-dimensional subspace T ⊆ ℝ^N, Hᵐ(T ∩ B(w, ρ)) = ω_m ρᵐ for w ∈ T and ρ > 0, with ω_m ∈ (0, ∞): T with the induced metric is an m-dimensional inner product space on which μHE[m] is the volume measure (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Measure.addHaar_ball).
0.4 Translation. For a ∈ ℝ^N let A_a := A − a = {b − a : b ∈ A} (compact, Hⁿ(A_a) = Hⁿ(A)). Since X_p(a, r, s) = a + X_p(0, r, s), m(a, p, r, s) = Hⁿ(A_a ∩ X_p(0, r, s)); and Ax(a, p) holds iff some b′ ∈ A_a has b′ ≠ 0, |b′| < δ, p b′ = 0. Hence T(a, p) for A is the same statement as T(0, p) for the set A_a (below, "T(0, p) for A″" means the three conditions at the point 0 with A″ in place of A).

1. Borel measurability (parent 8a).
1.1 Lemma. Let Ξ be a metrizable space, U ⊆ Ξ × ℝ^N open and ν a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N. Then ξ ↦ ν(U_ξ), U_ξ := {x : (ξ, x) ∈ U} (an open set), is lower semicontinuous on Ξ, hence Borel. Proof: let ξ_k → ξ. If x ∈ U_ξ then (ξ, x) lies in the open set U, so (ξ_k, x) ∈ U for all large k; hence 1_{U_ξ}(x) ≤ liminf_k 1_{U_{ξ_k}}(x) for every x. By Fatou's lemma, ν(U_ξ) ≤ ∫ liminf_k 1_{U_{ξ_k}} dν ≤ liminf_k ν(U_{ξ_k}). In a metrizable space sequential lower semicontinuity is lower semicontinuity, and {ξ : ν(U_ξ) > t} is then open.
1.2 Apply 1.1 with Ξ := ℝ^N × 𝓛 × ℝ × ℝ, ν := μ_A and U := {((a, p, r, s), x) : |p(x − a)| < s|x − a| and |x − a| < r} (open: strict inequalities between continuous functions). Since m(a, p, r, s) = μ_A(U_{(a,p,r,s)}), m is lower semicontinuous, hence Borel, on Ξ.
1.3 Monotonicity and left continuity. For fixed (a, p), m(a, p, r, s) is nondecreasing in r and in s. If r_k ↑ r and s_k ↑ s are increasing sequences with 0 < r_k < r and 0 < s_k < s, then X_p(a, r_k, s_k) increases to X_p(a, r, s) (a point x with |x − a| < r and |p(x − a)| < s|x − a| has |x − a| > 0, hence |x − a| < r_k and |p(x − a)| < s_k|x − a| for large k), so m(a, p, r_k, s_k) ↑ m(a, p, r, s) by continuity from below of μ_A.
1.4 Countable forms. Let ℚ₊ := ℚ ∩ (0, ∞).

2. Sphere lemma (parent 8b; Dall'Alba Lemma 4.15 and Theorem 4.16 on the sphere).
2.0 Setting. Let H ⊆ ℝ^N be an (n+1)-dimensional subspace with orthogonal projection p_H, S(H) := {θ ∈ H : |θ| = 1}, and σ_H(E) := Hⁿ(E ∩ S(H)) for Borel E (a finite Borel measure by 2.1(c)). Let A′ ⊆ ℝ^N be compact with Hⁿ(A′) < ∞. For θ ∈ S(H) and s > 0 put Z_θ(s) := {x : |p_Hx − (p_Hx·θ)θ| < s|p_Hx|} (the slab cone with axis ℝθ ⊕ H^⊥; |y − (y·θ)θ| = dist(y, ℝθ); p_Hx ≠ 0 on Z_θ(s)), m′(θ, r, s) := Hⁿ(A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Z_θ(s)), and

 Ψ∞(θ): ∀K ∈ ℝ ∀ε > 0 ∃s ∈ (0, ε) ∃r ∈ (0, δ): K(rs)ⁿ ≤ m′(θ, r, s);
 Ax′(θ): ∃x ∈ A′ with x ≠ 0, |x| < δ and p_Hx ∈ ℝθ.
 Call θ good for (H, A′, δ) if Ψ0(θ) ∨ Ψ∞(θ) ∨ Ax′(θ).

2.1 Sphere estimates. Fix ζ ∈ S(H); let T_ζ := H ∩ ζ^⊥ (n-dimensional) with orthogonal projection π_ζ (1-Lipschitz, π_ζζ = 0), and Γ(w) := w + (1 − |w|²)^{1/2}ζ for w ∈ T_ζ with |w| ≤ 1. Γ maps the closed unit ball of T_ζ bijectively onto {ξ ∈ S(H) : ξ·ζ ≥ 0}, with inverse π_ζ.
 (a) σ_H(B(ζ, ρ)) ≥ ω_n(ρ/2)ⁿ for 0 < ρ ≤ 2. If w ∈ T_ζ and |w| < ρ/2 (≤ 1), then, since 1 − (1 − t)^{1/2} ≤ t for t ∈ [0, 1], |Γ(w) − ζ|² = |w|² + (1 − (1 − |w|²)^{1/2})² ≤ |w|² + |w|⁴ ≤ 2|w|² < ρ². So T_ζ ∩ B(0, ρ/2) ⊆ π_ζ(S(H) ∩ B(ζ, ρ)), and as π_ζ is 1-Lipschitz, Hⁿ(S(H) ∩ B(ζ, ρ)) ≥ Hⁿ(T_ζ ∩ B(0, ρ/2)) = ω_n(ρ/2)ⁿ (0.3).

On {w ∈ T_ζ : |w| ≤ 1/2} the function w ↦ (1 − |w|²)^{1/2} has gradient of norm |w|(1 − |w|²)^{−1/2} ≤ 1/√3 < 1, so it is 1-Lipschitz there (convex domain) and Γ is 2-Lipschitz there. Hence Hⁿ(S(H) ∩ B(ζ, ρ)) ≤ 2ⁿHⁿ(T_ζ ∩ B(0, ρ)) = 2ⁿω_nρⁿ.

Thus σ_H(B(ζ, ρ)) ≤ C₁ρⁿ for all ζ ∈ S(H) and ρ > 0, where C₁ := 2ⁿ max(ω_n, Hⁿ(S(H))); also σ_H(B̄(ζ, ρ)) ≤ σ_H(B(ζ, 2ρ)) ≤ 2ⁿC₁ρⁿ. Put c₁ := 2^{−n}ω_n, so σ_H(B(ζ, ρ)) ≥ c₁ρⁿ for 0 < ρ ≤ 2.
2.2 An outer measure on S(H). For E ⊆ S(H) let Λ(E) := {x ∈ ℝ^N : p_Hx ≠ 0 and (p_Hx/|p_Hx| ∈ E or −p_Hx/|p_Hx| ∈ E)} and μ(E) := sup_{0<r<δ} r^{−n}Hⁿ(A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Λ(E)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Then μ(∅) = 0, μ is monotone, and μ(⋃_i E_i) ≤ Σ_i μ(E_i) for countably many E_i, because Λ(⋃_i E_i) = ⋃_i Λ(E_i), Hⁿ is countably subadditive for each fixed r, and a supremum of countably subadditive monotone set functions is countably subadditive and monotone.
2.3 The axis set. C := {θ ∈ S(H) : Ax′(θ)} = ⋃_{j ≥ 1} π₁(K_j) with K_j := {(θ, x) ∈ S(H) × A′ : 1/j ≤ |x| ≤ δ − 1/j, p_Hx − (p_Hx·θ)θ = 0} (closed in the compact S(H) × A′, hence compact), so C is σ-compact and Borel. Moreover μ(S(H) ∖ C) = 0: if E ⊆ S(H) ∖ C, r ∈ (0, δ) and x ∈ A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Λ(E), then x ≠ 0 (as p_Hx ≠ 0), |x| < δ, and p_Hx ∈ ℝθ for the point θ := ±p_Hx/|p_Hx| ∈ E; so θ ∈ C, contradicting E ∩ C = ∅. Hence A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Λ(E) = ∅ for all r ∈ (0, δ), and μ(E) = 0.
2.4 Caps versus slab cones. For unit vectors ξ, θ: dist(ξ, ℝθ) ≤ |ξ − θ|, and if ξ·θ ≥ 0 then |ξ − θ|² = 2(1 − ξ·θ) ≤ 2(1 − (ξ·θ)²) = 2dist(ξ, ℝθ)², so |ξ − θ| ≤ 2dist(ξ, ℝθ). Consequently, for θ ∈ S(H) and s, t > 0: Z_θ(s) ⊆ Λ(S(H) ∩ B(θ, 2s)) [for x ∈ Z_θ(s), y := p_Hx ≠ 0, the point ξ := ±y/|y| with ξ·θ ≥ 0 satisfies |ξ − θ| ≤ 2dist(ξ, ℝθ) = 2dist(y, ℝθ)/|y| < 2s], and Λ(S(H) ∩ B(θ, t)) ⊆ Z_θ(t) [if ξ := ±y/|y| ∈ B(θ, t) then dist(y, ℝθ)/|y| = dist(ξ, ℝθ) ≤ |ξ − θ| < t]. Given K and ε > 0 (if K ≤ 0, any s ∈ (0, ε), r ∈ (0, δ) works), take t ∈ (0, ε) with μ(S(H) ∩ B(θ, t)) > Ktⁿ; by definition of μ there is r ∈ (0, δ) with Hⁿ(A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Λ(S(H) ∩ B(θ, t))) > K(rt)ⁿ, so m′(θ, r, t) > K(rt)ⁿ; take s := t.

2.6 Proof of the sphere lemma. F := S(H) ∖ C is Borel with μ(F) = 0 (2.3). By 2.5 there is a σ_H-null set N₀ (which may be taken Borel, by passing to a Borel σ_H-null superset) such that every θ ∈ F ∖ N₀ satisfies the hypothesis of (α) or of (β), hence Ψ0(θ) or Ψ∞(θ) (2.4). Every θ ∈ C satisfies Ax′(θ). So every θ ∈ S(H) ∖ N₀ is good.

Hence ∫φ dν = Ψ_φ(e_{n+1}) is the same for every such ν. Two finite Borel measures on the compact metric space S⁰ with equal integrals of all continuous functions are equal; so ν₀ = σ̄.

Indeed p_{hH⁰} = hp_{H⁰}hᵀ, so the slab cone of (hH⁰, hθ) with parameter s is h·Z_θ(s) (slab cone of (H⁰, θ)); B(0, r) = hB(0, r); Hⁿ(A′ ∩ h(B(0, r) ∩ Z_θ(s))) = Hⁿ(h^{−1}A′ ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Z_θ(s)) (Hⁿ is invariant under h^{−1}); and x ∈ A′, x ≠ 0, |x| < δ, p_{hH⁰}x ∈ ℝhθ iff y := h^{−1}x ∈ h^{−1}A′, y ≠ 0, |y| < δ, p_{H⁰}y ∈ ℝθ. The set h^{−1}A′ is compact with Hⁿ(h^{−1}A′) = Hⁿ(A′) < ∞, so the sphere lemma (Step 2, applied to H⁰ and h^{−1}A′) gives a σ_{H⁰}-null Borel set N_h ⊆ ℝ^N containing every θ ∈ S⁰ that is not good for (H⁰, h^{−1}A′, δ). By 4.4: ∫_{O′}χ(hg′) dθ′(g′) = θ′({g′ : g′e_{n+1} is not good for (H⁰, h^{−1}A′, δ)}) ≤ θ′({g′ : g′e_{n+1} ∈ N_h}) = ν₀(N_h) = σ̄(N_h) = 0.
4.6 Fubini. (h, g′) ↦ χ(hg′) is Borel on O(N) × O′. By right invariance, ∫_{O(N)}χ(h) dθ_N(h) = ∫_{O(N)}χ(hg′) dθ_N(h) for each g′ ∈ O′. Integrating over g′ (θ′ is a probability) and using Tonelli: ∫χ dθ_N = ∫_{O′}∫_{O(N)}χ(hg′) dθ_N(h) dθ′(g′) = ∫_{O(N)}∫_{O′}χ(hg′) dθ′(g′) dθ_N(h) = 0 by 4.5. So θ_N(B_1) = 0, hence θ_N(B_j) = 0 for all j (4.3) and θ_N({g : not T(a, gP₀gᵀ)}) = 0 (4.1). This holds for every a ∈ A.
4.7 Tonelli over A × O(N). The set 𝒩′ of 1.5(c) is Borel; its section at a is {g : not T(a, gP₀gᵀ)} if a ∈ A and ∅ otherwise. By Tonelli for the finite measures μ_A and θ_N: ∫_{O(N)}μ_A({a : (a, g) ∈ 𝒩′}) dθ_N(g) = ∫_{ℝ^N}θ_N({g : (a, g) ∈ 𝒩′}) dμ_A(a) = 0 by 4.6, and {a : (a, g) ∈ 𝒩′} = 𝒩^{gP₀gᵀ}. Hence Hⁿ(𝒩^{gP₀gᵀ}) = 0 for θ_N-a.e. g, i.e. θ_N(𝒢̃) = 0 (𝒢̃ as in 1.5(c)).

5. Transfer to Lebesgue-a.e. frames (parent 9) and conclusion.
5.1 For g ∈ O(N) and v ∈ (ℝ^N)ⁿ put g·v := (gv_1, …, gv_n). The map (g, v) ↦ g·v is continuous, and λ is invariant under v ↦ g·v: each factor's volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) is invariant under the linear isometry g (|det g| = 1), hence so is the product measure. If v ∈ 𝒱 then g·v ∈ 𝒱, span(g·v) = g·span(v), and P_{g·v} = gP_vgᵀ; if v ∉ 𝒱 then g·v ∉ 𝒱.
5.2 For v ∈ 𝒱 choose h ∈ O(N) with hW₀ = span v (send e_1, …, e_n to an orthonormal basis of span v and e_{n+1}, …, e_N to one of its orthogonal complement); then P_v = hP₀hᵀ and P_{g·v} = (gh)P₀(gh)ᵀ. Hence {g : g·v ∈ 𝒮} = {g : gh ∈ 𝒢̃} = 𝒢̃h^{−1}, and θ_N({g : g·v ∈ 𝒮}) = θ_N(𝒢̃) = 0 by right invariance and 4.7. For v ∉ 𝒱 this set is empty because 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒱.
5.3 The set {(g, v) : g·v ∈ 𝒮} ⊆ O(N) × (ℝ^N)ⁿ is Borel (1.5(b), 5.1). Using invariance (λ({v : g·v ∈ 𝒮}) = λ(𝒮) for every g), θ_N(O(N)) = 1, Tonelli (θ_N finite, λ σ-finite) and 5.2:
 λ(𝒮) = ∫_{O(N)}λ({v : g·v ∈ 𝒮}) dθ_N(g) = ∫_{(ℝ^N)ⁿ}θ_N({g : g·v ∈ 𝒮}) dλ(v) = 0.
5.4 Conclusion. 𝒮 = {v ∈ 𝒱 : Hⁿ({a ∈ A : not T(a, P_v)}) > 0} is λ-null. Hence for λ-a.e. v ∈ (ℝ^N)ⁿ: if v is linearly independent, then μHE[n] {a | a ∈ A ∧ ¬ T(a, frameProjection v)} = 0, where T(a, p) is precisely the disjunction Φ0 ∨ Φ∞ ∨ Ax written in the Lean statement (cone {x | ‖p (x − a)‖ < s * ‖x − a‖} ∩ Metric.ball a r, bounds ENNReal.ofReal (c * (r * s) ^ n) and ENNReal.ofReal (K * (r * s) ^ n), axis condition ∃ b ∈ A, b ≠ a ∧ dist b a < δ ∧ p (b − a) = 0). This is ForAlmostAllProjections (n + ℓ) n (fun p ↦ μHE[n] {a | a ∈ A ∧ ¬ T(a, p)} = 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Measurability: cone masses are lower semicontinuous in (a, p, r, s) (Fatou), monotone and left continuous, so Φ0, Φ∞ have rational forms; the axis condition is σ-compact; the exceptional set 𝒩 ⊆ ℝ^N × 𝓛 is Borel.

Sphere lemma: for an (n+1)-plane H the outer measure μ(E) = sup_r r^{−n}Hⁿ(A′ ∩ B(0,r) ∩ Λ(E)) vanishes off the σ-compact axis set; a density dichotomy for μ on S(H) (closed F_j, 5r-covering, sphere estimates, Besicovitch density) and the cap/slab-cone comparison give goodness for Hⁿ-a.e. θ ∈ S(H).
Slab cones versus cones: Z_{u_j}(s) ⊆ X(0, V, s) ⊆ ⋃_j Z_{u_j}(s*), s* ≤ √ℓ s; if all ℓ slab directions u_j are good then the trichotomy T holds.

Haar averaging over O(N): reduce to j = 1 by a permutation; the law of g′e_{n+1} under the Haar measure of O′ ≅ O(n+1) is normalized Hⁿ on the sphere (uniqueness of invariant probabilities); coset invariance, the sphere lemma and Fubini with right invariance give θ_N-null bad sets; Tonelli over A × O(N).
Transfer: Lebesgue measure on frames is O(N)-invariant; Tonelli and right invariance turn the θ_N-null set of bad planes into a Lebesgue-null set of frames.

subproblems.title: Besicovitch–Federer for compact purely unrectifiable sets of finite measure, given Eilenberg's inequality (Dall'Alba, proof of Thm 5.1)

Then for all n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1 and every compact, purely n-unrectifiable A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(A) < ∞: for Lebesgue-a.e. v ∈ (ℝ^{n+ℓ})ⁿ, if v is linearly independent then Hⁿ(frameProjection v(A)) = 0, i.e. ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p(A)) = 0).

subproblems.title: Reduction to compact sets: σ-finite purely unrectifiable sets are covered by a null set and countably many compact purely unrectifiable sets of finite measure
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and Q ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} be purely n-unrectifiable with Q = ⋃_j Q_j and Hⁿ(Q_j) < ∞ for all j. Then there are Z ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 and sets K_i (i ∈ ℕ), each compact, purely n-unrectifiable and with Hⁿ(K_i) < ∞, such that Q ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_i K_i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (Q : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))), PurelyUnrectifiable n Q → (∃ Qj : ℕ → Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), Q = ⋃ j, Qj j ∧ ∀ j, μHE[n] (Qj j) < ∞) → ∃ (Z : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))) (K : ℕ → Set (Rn (n + ℓ))), μHE[n] Z = 0 ∧ (∀ i, IsCompact (K i) ∧ PurelyUnrectifiable n (K i) ∧ μHE[n] (K i) < ∞) ∧ Q ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃ i, K i
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 1 of the parent proof (its adaptation (a)): Borel hulls, the measurable case of Simon's Lemma 3.2 as formalized in SimonGMT (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.measurable_rectifiable_purelyUnrectifiable_decomposition, pinned dependency, not the sibling node, so no dependency cycle arises), and inner regularity of Hⁿ on Borel sets of finite measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(2), 1.16).

Notation. N := n + ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] (outer measure), Q = ⋃_j Q_j with Hⁿ(Q_j) < ∞, Q purely n-unrectifiable.

1. Borel hulls. For each j let B_j := toMeasurable Hⁿ Q_j: a Borel set with Q_j ⊆ B_j and Hⁿ(B_j) = Hⁿ(Q_j) < ∞ (Mathlib subset_toMeasurable, measurableSet_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable).

2. Decomposition of B_j. B_j is Borel, hence Hⁿ-null-measurable, and B_j ⊆ ⋃_k S_k with S_k := B_j for all k, Hⁿ(S_k) < ∞. By the SimonGMT measurable form of Lemma 3.2 there are R_j, P_j with B_j = R_j ∪ P_j, R_j ∩ P_j = ∅, R_j Borel, R_j countably n-rectifiable and P_j purely n-unrectifiable. Since the union is disjoint, P_j = B_j ∖ R_j, which is Borel; Hⁿ(P_j) ≤ Hⁿ(B_j) < ∞.

3. The rectifiable part of Q_j is null. Q_j ∩ R_j ⊆ Q (because Q_j ⊆ ⋃_k Q_k = Q), and Q_j ∩ R_j is countably n-rectifiable as a subset of R_j (CountablyRectifiable.mono). Since Q is purely n-unrectifiable, Hⁿ(Q_j ∩ R_j) = 0.

4. Inner regularity. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is a Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^N, so it is inner regular by compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (Mathlib instance instInnerRegularCompactLTTopOfIsCompletelyPseudoMetrizableSpace, i.e. InnerRegularCompactLTTop; MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_diff_lt). Hence for every i ∈ ℕ there is a compact K_{j,i} ⊆ P_j with Hⁿ(P_j ∖ K_{j,i}) < 1/(i+1). Then Hⁿ(P_j ∖ ⋃_k K_{j,k}) ≤ Hⁿ(P_j ∖ K_{j,i}) < 1/(i+1) for every i, so Hⁿ(P_j ∖ ⋃_k K_{j,k}) = 0.

5. Properties of the K_{j,i}: each is compact; purely n-unrectifiable as a subset of the purely n-unrectifiable P_j (PurelyUnrectifiable.mono); and Hⁿ(K_{j,i}) ≤ Hⁿ(P_j) < ∞.

6. Definitions. Z := ⋃_j ((Q_j ∩ R_j) ∪ (P_j ∖ ⋃_i K_{j,i})); by 3, 4 and countable subadditivity, Hⁿ(Z) ≤ Σ_j (0 + 0) = 0. Enumerate the countable family (K_{j,i})_{(j,i) ∈ ℕ×ℕ} as (K_m)_{m ∈ ℕ} via a bijection ℕ ≃ ℕ × ℕ (e.g. K_m := K_{(Nat.unpair m).1, (Nat.unpair m).2}).

7. Covering. Let x ∈ Q. Then x ∈ Q_j for some j, so x ∈ B_j = R_j ∪ P_j. If x ∈ R_j, then x ∈ Q_j ∩ R_j ⊆ Z. If x ∈ P_j, then either x ∈ K_{j,i} for some i, i.e. x ∈ K_m for m := Nat.pair j i, or x ∈ P_j ∖ ⋃_i K_{j,i} ⊆ Z. Hence Q ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_m K_m, and Z, (K_m) have all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace each Q_j by a Borel hull B_j of the same finite measure.
Decompose B_j = R_j ⊔ P_j by SimonGMT's measurable Lemma 3.2 (R_j Borel rectifiable, P_j Borel purely unrectifiable); Q_j ∩ R_j ⊆ Q is rectifiable, hence null.
Inner regularity of Hⁿ on Borel sets of finite measure: compact K_{j,i} ⊆ P_j exhaust P_j up to a null set.
Z := ⋃_j((Q_j ∩ R_j) ∪ (P_j ∖ ⋃_i K_{j,i})) is null and Q ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃ K_{j,i}; re-index by ℕ.
